subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Cambridge IGCSE IGCSE Literature in English specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: Close attention to poetic language and imagery sharpens the analysis of narrative voice and style in prose
Reading prose for character and theme transfers to drama, with added attention to performance and dramatic form
The sensitivity to rhythm, tone and figurative language built on poetry illuminates dramatic verse and dialogue
Analysing set poems develops the independent close-reading instinct required for unseen passages
Prose analysis builds the skills students apply unsupported to unseen prose or in coursework essays
Studying drama equips students to handle unseen dramatic extracts or extended coursework on a play
